name: Glendo State Park (Mule Hill Campground)
note: Mule Hill is a small campground on the west shore of a bay of Glendo Reservoir, entered from Glendo Park Road about a quarter mile southeast of the main fee booth. Its gravel back-in pads run along the edge of a band of cottonwoods that lines the bay; at high water (early May to mid-July) the lake comes up into the trees, and later in the summer the bay drains out. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: reserve.wyoming.gov (US eDirect API wyordr.usedirect.com/wyomingrdr/rdr/, PlaceId 10 'Glendo State Park', FacilityId 339 'Mule Hill', facility point 42.48445,-105.00512, read 2026-11-20): 13 web-bookable units - 12 'Campsite Non-Electric' MH01-MH12 (IsRVSite true; 'Parking Pad Material' Gravel, MH07 Paved (ADA); 'Unit & Parking Size(ft)' 55-180 (MH02/MH08 55, MH06 60, MH09 70, MH03/MH05 75, MH10 80, MH01 95, MH12 125, MH11 140, MH04 155, MH07 180); pull-throughs MH04, MH07, MH11, the rest back-in; Rate 10.00; MaximumStay 14) + Group Site G13 (270 ft gravel pull-through) -> real drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits. Wyoming State Parks' own Mule Hill page (wyoparks.wyo.gov/index.php/about-our-campgrounds/1697-mule-hill-glendo, read as search-result text 2026-11-20; the site refuses with an F5 challenge) and its copies on The Dyrt and Campflare (read 2026-11-20): 'Mule Hill is a small campground with only 13 campsites', main entrance 'on the left hand side of Glendo Park Road, 1/4 mile southeast of the Main Fee Booth', 'All campsites in Mule Hill are developed, with gravel road access and established parking pads', 'Site 7 has a large, ADA compliant, cement pad'. No 4WD or sand wording on the park's text (unlike Broken Arrow). Imagery 2026-11-20: gravel loop roads and spurs off the paved park road, a toilet building by MH02/MH03. Not in the DB: no name match; nearest entry 13969 Custer Cove ~1.9 km E (FacilityId 336), a separate facility; next 13977 Reno Cove ~3 km. Public (state): no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World Imagery frames at 400 m and 110 m half-widths (0.8 and 0.22 m/px) with every reserve.wyoming.gov unit point (grid MapInfo, FacilityId 339) plotted; all images rendered. Imagery is leaf-off with the reservoir below full pool (open water 60-100 m east of the pads). Glendo full pool 4635.0 ft = 1413.51 m NAVD88 (glendo_notes.txt). USGS 3DEP lidar (epqs.nationalmap.gov): unit points MH01 1417.4, MH02 1417.3, MH03 1417.1, MH04 1416.8, MH05 1416.6, MH06 1415.5, MH07 1415.5, MH08 1414.3, MH09 1414.2, MH10 1414.6, MH11 1415.0, MH12 1414.6, G13 1421.6 m; hydro-flattened water surface 1412.98 m. Profiles at 5 m steps on bearings 45/90/135 to the first point at or below full pool: MH01 25 m NE/E, 30 m SE; MH02 20 m NE/E; MH03 15 m E, 20 m NE; MH05 15 m E; MH06 15 m NE/E; MH08 15 m E; MH09 15 m E/SE; MH10 15 m NE, 20 m SE; MH12 20 m SE; MH04 50 m and MH11 50 m E; MH07 45 m E (back from the loop). Ground check: every lakeward pad (MH01-MH03, MH05, MH06, MH08-MH10, MH12) ends at the inland edge of a continuous, dense cottonwood stand ~30-45 m deep that lines the bay, and the full-pool line falls inside that stand - the park's own text: 'from early May to Mid-July, campers at Mule Hill will find easy access to the water, which comes up into the trees. After July, the bay drains out'; a 2025-10-29 Dyrt review of the group site: 'a wooded area between the site and the reservoir'. A continuous treeline between pad and water is a buffer -> not lakefront; the water at high pool sits 15-25 m from the pads among the trunks, so a filtered view -> lakeview (as 15740 Indian Point's IP04-IP12, the same cottonwood setting). MH04, MH07 and MH11 sit back on open grass west of the loop, MH07/MH11 exposed, with the tree band between them and the bay; G13 is on the hill to the north. Engine tags every unit 'Waterfront Setting: Reservoir' (type-level). Not below the dam: the pads stand 0.7-3.9 m above full pool on the reservoir side.

flags: Waterfront held at lakeview: the lidar puts the full-pool line 15-25 m from most lakeward pads, but inside a continuous dense cottonwood stand (~30-45 m deep) that the park itself says the water 'comes up into' - a treeline buffer, the same call as 15740 Indian Point IP04-IP12. Lakefront would rest on the park's 'easy access to the water' wording; not waterfront would rest on the trees screening the view in leaf. Lakeview is the middle, default-down reading.

Season of the water: the park says the water reaches the trees only early May to mid-July; 'After July, the bay drains out, and the closest water access is through the south side of Whiskey Gulch Campground.'

Reservation dates: The Dyrt's copy says 'Reservations Required May 1 through September 30'; the engine's SeasonDates and the park's Glendo page (2026-10-12 capture) say May 15 - Sep 15 - written as the engine.

Access: The Dyrt's page carries 'Access involves rough roads leading to the elevated site', which reads as its 2025-10-29 review of the group site G13 (a cul-de-sac on the hill) - G13 sits on the hill north of the loop (lidar 1421.6 m, ~6 m above the pads); reviewer wording, not the park's; the park says gravel road access and established pads for all sites.
